lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the edge of town, the old Harbor Biscuit Works sits derelict. The sign still reads RISE & SHINE. Someone has been here before you.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Your grandfather and I started here, dear. One oven, one table, and a firm belief that the town deserved better toast.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: We outgrew it, then we lost it, and I've spent a lot of years pretending I didn't mind. I minded. Let's bring her back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inside, the machines sleep under a century of dust. Somewhere in the rafters a lone pigeon files an objection.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A figure in oily overalls crawls out from under the conveyor belt holding a wrench like a trophy.

lines.speaker: bex
lines.text: Bex. Engineer. I've been fixing this line for free for three weeks, because nobody told me it wasn't mine.

lines.speaker: bex
lines.text: It wants to run. You can hear it. I just need a few things welded, a few things oiled, and a very forgiving fire inspector.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Hire her, dear. Anyone who fixes machines for free has a better reason than money.

lines.speaker: bex
lines.text: Also: chocolate. I read that the old recipe book has chocolate in it. I would like to be involved in that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in a white hard hat and a magnificent moustache appears in the doorway, as if the building had summoned him.

lines.speaker: dill
lines.text: Foreman Dill. Thirty-four years on this floor. I'd retired. I came by to see the old girl one more time.

lines.speaker: dill
lines.text: ...Is that a conveyor belt that moves? Who authorized that? I'll need a hat for you, and a clipboard, and a lot of coffee.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Dill ran the night shift when we were kids. Nobody ever shouted louder, and nobody ever cared more.

lines.speaker: dill
lines.text: Safety first, quality second, shouting third. I'll start with the shouting.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A woman with round glasses and a very full notebook sneaks around a pillar, loudly, writing as she goes.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Moss. Harbor Herald. Rumour is a little bakery is turning an abandoned factory into something. Also that MegaBun is 'concerned'.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: I do not take sides. I take notes. Though I did eat four of your scones, which is a form of bias, and I'll declare it.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: A good reporter is a customer who writes things down, dear. Be honest with her and she'll be honest with the town.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: Quote of the week: 'MegaBun is delighted to have noticed.' I've decided that's their slogan.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The control room hums. A bank of dials, a steel cabinet the size of a fridge, and a small green screen that blinks on as you walk in.

lines.speaker: bex
lines.text: Meet the Auto-Oven. It watches the bake, collects the batch, loads the next. It never gets bored. I've asked. It said 'beep'.

lines.speaker: bex
lines.text: It still needs ingredients on the board, and someone to decide what it bakes. It does the work. You do the thinking.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Machines are fine, dear, so long as somebody who loves the baking decides what goes in them.

lines.speaker: dill
lines.text: I'll be watching that thing. It has a very trusting face. I do not trust it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The visitor gallery opens and half the town files in: the fruit seller, the ferry captain, a very large fishmonger, the terrace crowd.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.text: I counted two hundred. Two hundred people came to see a factory. This hasn't happened since the Biscuit Works opened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in a trench coat and sunglasses tries to blend in with a rubber plant. It is not working. He waves.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Wren, dear. Good morning. Would you like a scone? You don't have to pretend it's for research.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Outside, a convoy of orange vans is parked at the gate. They have not been invited. They are very, very polite about it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Behind the old time clock, in a biscuit tin soldered shut for forty years, the last page of Grandma's recipe book. It is a single line.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: I wondered where I'd put that. It says: 'Bake for the people who show up. The rest takes care of itself.'

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: I wrote it the day your grandfather and I signed the lease on this place. We didn't have a penny. We had every single person on the street.

lines.speaker: bex
lines.text: That's the whole book. Every page. It's complete.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Five pages, one book, one town. The recipe book closes with a satisfied thump. A pigeon, somewhere, sighs with relief.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At noon the doors swing open. Chad Crustworth enters in a very expensive suit, with Buns-A-Lot a respectful three paces behind.

lines.speaker: chad
lines.text: PRESS RELEASE: MegaBun is delighted to announce that it has noticed this factory, this brand, and this wonderful little town.

lines.speaker: chad
lines.text: We would like to buy you. All of it. The recipes, the shop, the harbor stall. We'll keep the name. We'll replace the bread.

lines.speaker: bunsalot
lines.text: Sorry about him. I made the cookies, and he's been telling people he did. I'd like to say I think your scones are better.

lines.speaker: chad
lines.text: The offer is generous. It contains the word 'synergy' eleven times. I have counted them. Please sign by close of business.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Take your time, dear. Offers expire. Recipes don't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The factory floor is full. Every regular, every neighbour, every helper. The ferry captain is blocking the exit with her cap in her hands.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You tear Chad's offer in half, then in quarters, then gently feed the pieces to the Auto-Oven. It beeps. It looks, somehow, pleased.

lines.speaker: chad
lines.text: This is unprecedented. We have never been refused. I will need to consult the committee.

lines.speaker: mrs-crustworth
lines.text: Charles. Sit down. I tasted their scone at the contest. It was better than yours. I told you. Go home and make something honest.

lines.speaker: chad
lines.text: ...Mother. Yes, Mother.

lines.speaker: bunsalot
lines.text: I quit, by the way! Is there a job here? I can fold boxes. I'm very good at boxes.

lines.speaker: trevor
lines.text: Welcome to the family. There's tea.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Look at them all, dear. One little shop, one big town, and a book that's finally whole. Now put the kettle on. The ovens are warm.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Rise & Shine Factory opens. The sun rises over the harbor, the first bake leaves the line, and the whole town smells like toast.
